fail_to_pass.name: paging_through_an_affected_store_list_over_a_static_dataset
fail_to_pass.description:
Paging through an affected store list over a static dataset in which many rows
tie on the displayed ordering returns every row exactly once across the full
set of pages — no omissions and no duplicates. Pre-fix, tied rows reorder
between page requests under LIMIT/OFFSET so paging drops and repeats rows.

fail_to_pass.name: paging_the_issues_list_across_multiple_projects_—_where_issu
fail_to_pass.description:
Paging the issues list across multiple projects — where issue identifiers
collide between projects because they are assigned per project — returns every
issue exactly once. This is the headline cross-project symptom.

fail_to_pass.name: a_batch_of_issue_comments_created_together_is_read_back_by_t
fail_to_pass.description:
A batch of issue comments created together is read back by the comment list in
the order it was inserted. Pre-fix, a batch shares one transaction timestamp,
so after any read-side tiebreak the order falls back to a random UUID and the
batch is scrambled.

fail_to_pass.name: the_fix_addresses_the_defect_as_a_class_across_the_store's_o
fail_to_pass.description:
The fix addresses the defect as a class across the store's offset-paginated
list functions, not only the single list named in the symptom report.

pass_to_pass.name: a_caller-supplied_explicit_ordering_is_still_honored:_the_fi
pass_to_pass.description:
A caller-supplied explicit ordering is still honored: the fix only breaks ties
and never overrides the requested lead sort.

pass_to_pass.name: lists_that_were_already_total_are_not_needlessly_rewritten,
pass_to_pass.description:
Lists that were already total are not needlessly rewritten, and the change
does not alter the leading sort semantics any caller depends on (only ties are
broken). Guards against a spurious broad rewrite.

pass_to_pass.name: each_appended_tiebreak_is_unique_under_its_query's_scope_and
pass_to_pass.description:
Each appended tiebreak is unique under its query's scope and its sort
direction matches the leading key and an existing index, so ordering is total
without defeating the index that keeps paging cheap.
